description: Stage 12 completes the matrix wh dependency. Relation 1 moves who3 to the new matrix specifier who4 under a new C′ (mcbar) that wraps the existing C head and TP. Relation 2, a chain claim, also recovers movements into who4 from the earlier intermediate copies who2 and who1. While relation 2 was still pending, its landing wrapper was collapsed at relation 1's moment, withdrawing who4 and mcbar again: the movement step changed nothing and the landing, C′ and arrow appeared with relation 2. A landing an active relation has introduced is no longer withdrawn by a later claim about it.
source: GPT-6.1 Sol, high reasoning, Codex OAuth qualification run with the character spell-out contract (character-spellout-v3), 19 October 2026 (night3 batch, 59-en-wh-island, analysis 1), commit bcf1b56. Tokens are the shared word list of that run.
sentence: Who do you wonder whether Mary saw?

derivationStages.stageRecord: Externally merge saw with the interrogative pronoun Who. The pronoun is the internal argument of see and receives its theme interpretation here. Proper names and pronouns are treated as minimal nominal objects headed by D. Throughout, repeated category labels identify projections of the same head under Bare Phrase Structure; they do not introduce an independently stipulated X-bar template. This is the beginning of the extraction analysis required by the input, not a repair of its eventual wh-island configuration.
derivationStages.statement: Build the embedded transitive predicate and its interrogative object.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge transitive little v with the verbal object, then externally merge Mary as its external argument. Mary receives the perceiver role associated with seeing. Transitive little v licenses accusative Case on the object Who. Both nominals remain in their first-merged positions at this stage.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the embedded external argument and transitive little v.

relations.relation: A-bar movement to a phase edge

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge Who at an outer edge of the embedded v projection. This provides an accessible occurrence for subsequent long-distance extraction under the Phase Impenetrability Condition. The object occurrence already displayed inside the verbal projection becomes an unpronounced copy; the new edge occurrence is currently pronounced. This is A-bar movement and does not replace Mary's external-argument position.
derivationStages.statement: Move the object to the embedded v-phase edge.

relations.relation: finite subject agreement and Case licensing

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge silent past T above the embedded v projection. T agrees with Mary, licenses nominative Case, and attracts Mary to its subject edge. The accusative-licensed wh object is not an active competitor for this nominative dependency. The first-merged occurrence of Mary becomes silent. This analysis retains saw as the inflected lexical V: past T licenses that form without syntactic V-to-T movement, and T has no separate pronunciation.
derivationStages.statement: Build the embedded finite clause and raise Mary.

values.scopeOfWho: not licensed as an embedded constituent question

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge whether as the overt embedded interrogative C selecting the finite clause. On this analysis whether is a head, not a nominal occupying the position through which Who must pass. It contributes embedded polar-question force; it does not give Who embedded constituent-question scope. The presence of this interrogative C is nevertheless crucial: subsequent extraction will cross a wh-island boundary.
derivationStages.statement: Introduce the embedded polar interrogative headed by whether.

relations.relation: A-bar movement to the embedded C edge

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge Who from the already established embedded v edge to an outer edge of the whether projection. Its former edge occurrence becomes silent. This analysis allows a general escape-edge feature on phase heads, including interrogative C, so phase accessibility alone does not prohibit the step. That assumption does not remove the wh-island restriction: the escape occurrence is not an embedded question operator licensed by whether, and extraction beyond this interrogative domain remains subject to an island assessment.
derivationStages.statement: Provide a successive-cyclic occurrence at the embedded C edge.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Externally merge wonder with the embedded interrogative projection. Wonder selects a question-denoting complement, so the whether clause is its selected complement rather than an adjunct or a relative clause. Merge matrix little v and introduce you as the experiencer of wondering. The wh dependency still originates as the object of saw; wonder supplies no alternative object position for Who.
derivationStages.statement: Embed the whether question under wonder and introduce you.

relations.relation: A-bar movement to the matrix v edge

values.configuration: extraction from a selected polar interrogative

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge Who from the embedded C edge to the matrix v edge, silencing its embedded edge occurrence. Successive cyclicity preserves phase accessibility, but this step now establishes extraction out of the selected whether interrogative. It therefore creates the wh-island dependency characteristic of the exact input. In a grammar enforcing the wh-island restriction categorically, this attempted dependency is illicit; continuing the representation records the attempted parse rather than claiming that phase-edge movement repairs the island.
derivationStages.statement: Continue extraction into the matrix clause and expose the island dependency.

relations.relation: matrix subject agreement and Case licensing

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge finite auxiliary do in matrix T. The lexical choice of do supplies an overt tense-bearing auxiliary while wonder remains a bare lexical verb; the following root interrogative structure will license this otherwise unnecessary support auxiliary. T agrees with you, licenses nominative Case, and attracts you from its external-argument position to the matrix subject edge. The lower subject occurrence becomes silent. The spelling you does not distinguish singular from plural, so this derivation does not impose a number interpretation.
derivationStages.statement: Build the matrix finite clause with auxiliary do and the raised subject.

derivationStages.stageRecord: Merge a silent root interrogative C above the matrix finite clause. Unlike embedded whether, this C carries the constituent-question requirement that will attract Who and the root interrogative requirement that will attract the finite auxiliary. The overt auxiliary selected in T is thereby justified as interrogative do-support. Neither movement has occurred yet: their source occurrences remain visibly available in the workspace.

Internally merge the finite auxiliary from T into a complex C head, preceding the silent interrogative head. The T occurrence becomes an unpronounced copy, while the C occurrence of do is pronounced. This head movement produces subject–auxiliary inversion: the pronounced auxiliary now precedes the raised subject you. Lexical wonder remains in its original verbal position.
derivationStages.statement: Move finite do to matrix C.

values.interpretation: For which person x do you wonder whether Mary saw x?

values.judgment: degraded or unacceptable under restrictive judgments; variable tolerance for argument extraction
values.phaseEdges: successive cyclicity does not itself remove the island restriction

derivationStages.stageRecord: Internally merge Who from the matrix v edge to the outer edge of matrix C, silencing the former occurrence. Matrix C now licenses the constituent-question dependency, while the original object occurrence of Who supplies its thematic interpretation with saw. The pronounced terminals yield exactly Who do you wonder whether Mary saw. The resulting interpretation asks for the person such that you wonder whether Mary saw that person. Crucially, the dependency crosses the embedded whether question: this is a wh-island configuration, not a well-formed long-distance extraction from an ordinary declarative complement. It is degraded or excluded under restrictive standard-English judgments, although argument extraction across a weak wh island is variably tolerated across speakers and contexts. That judgment variation does not introduce a second structural reading. In a categorical island grammar, this final tree is the completed representation of an unsuccessful derivational attempt, not a claim of grammatical convergence.
derivationStages.statement: Complete the matrix wh dependency and assess the exact sentence.
